assumptions: The customer's 'juniors' are the people whose changes go through this workspace's definitions, so stored-definition checks are the right place to enforce.
Advisory enforcement is acceptable for a first pass; the customer will flip to blocking after reviewing findings.
No existing object should be exempt via a legacy tag, since none has been identified as a deliberate legacy case.
The 'missing error handling' complaint maps to api.request calls outside try_catch.
confusions: The skill text says a 'legacy' tag is needed for except_tags, but the recipe lists it as a 'tag' build; it was not clear whether a tag must exist as an object or is just a string on objects. I did not create one.
The recipe names no build step beyond the legacy tag for code_review_basics, so the recipe gives no enforcement object for this goal; reasonable, but a reader may expect something to be built.
Template limit for functions (30 statements) is the same as for endpoints, which may be stricter than teams expect for functions; the template does not say so explicitly.
xano policy parse text output omits the severity line when severity is medium (it shows in -o json); looks like a display quirk, not a parse error.
wished_for: A worked example of mapping 'lines' to statements, since the customer's words are line counts.
A template or recipe variant that starts blocking only for new or changed objects, so existing violators do not block every merge.
An explicit note that the test rules check a test exists and asserts, not that its assertions are meaningful.
why_confidence: The six policies cover the three named complaints with real checks and parse cleanly, and the dry run is clean. Confidence is medium, not high, because error handling and test quality are only partly checkable, and the policies were not evaluated against the workspace (evaluate is forbidden for me), so I know from reading the files that acme_sync_shipping_rates and most endpoints would produce findings, but not the full finding list.
